articles.title: Dollar steady after Fed hold leaves rate path murky
articles.desc: After the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates steady, the US dollar found stability. Investors are now grappling with uncertainty regarding potential rate increases as inflation figures loom. The Fed highlighted robust economic growth, with Chair Kevin Warsh emphasizing the need for inflation control without hindering this progress. Eyes are now on upcoming central bank meetings in Europe and Japan, where rate adjustments are unlikely.

articles.desc: U.S. stock markets rallied following the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates steady. As inflation remains a concern, investors are recalibrating their outlook on potential future rate increases. The bond market showed fluctuations, particularly in the two-year Treasury yield post-announcement. Notably, several companies, such as GE HealthCare Technologies and Wendy's, reported better-than-expected earnings, leading to significant stock price surges.

articles.title: Gold dips on firmer dollar; US inflation data in focus
articles.desc: Gold prices experienced a decline as the dollar strengthened following the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady. Spot gold dropped by 0.7%, while both silver and platinum recorded slight downturns. However, palladium saw a modest uptick due to ongoing market volatility.

A notable decline in profit was attributed to an exceptional gain a year prior, while expenses rose sharply. The company plans to invest ₹35,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore annually in airports and data centres.

articles.title: US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as stubborn inflation puts future rate hikes in focus
articles.desc: The US Federal Reserve has decided to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged to evaluate inflation trends. Policymakers are assessing how high inflation might affect future monetary policy amid the upcoming midterm elections. Rising energy prices and tariffs contribute significantly to the ongoing inflation pressures faced by the economy. Traders are closely monitoring the upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report for indications of future rate hikes.

articles.desc: Here is what you need to know about the payment that millions will receive from January.

articles.title: World Bank sees commodity prices surging 23% in 2026 on Middle East war
articles.desc: Commodity prices were projected to rise 23% in 2026 as the Middle East war disrupted energy supplies and shipping, while grain disruptions and safe haven demand pushed food and metals prices higher. The World Bank warned that further conflict escalation and a severe El Niño could intensify inflation and food security risks.

articles.title: German startup NVision shows new path to quantum computing chips in Nature paper
articles.desc: Startups and tech giants such as Microsoft and IBM alike are racing to build quantum computers that hold the promise of solving problems that would take conventional machines thousands of years. But NVision, which has raised more than $155 million in funding from firms such as Abbott Laboratories, made the discovery published on Wednesday while working in an entirely different field: improving medical devices.

articles.title: Centre releases Rs 78 crore for senior citizens' welfare scheme
articles.desc: The ministry said it has released funds under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), a component of the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), for the financial year 2026-27.

articles.title: Karnataka, DGFT to host state-level workshop to help exporters leverage FTAs
articles.desc: On October 30, a workshop will be organized by the DGFT, Karnataka government, and FIEO in Bengaluru. The event aims to enhance Karnataka's export competitiveness and awareness of Free Trade Agreements. Nearly 200 participants, including exporters and industry officials, are expected to attend. Technical sessions will cover opportunities in various sectors and policy interventions under new FTAs. Senior officials and the state minister will address attendees at this important event.

articles.title: PM Modi to release Rs 18,680 crore under PM-Kisan scheme on October 30
articles.desc: On October 30, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to launch the 24th installment of the PM-Kisan scheme in Gujarat, aiming to support over 9.34 crore farmer families across the country with more than Rs 18,680 crore. In Gujarat alone, financial assistance surpassing Rs 1,051 crore will be granted to over 52.33 lakh farmer families.

articles.title: India only major emerging economy set to reduce debt ratio by 2031: RBI Deputy Governor
articles.desc: India is projected to be the only emerging market economy among nine economies with gross domestic product (GDP) exceeding USD 1 trillion to reduce its government debt-to-GDP ratio between 2025 and 2031, Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said, highlighting the country's stronger fiscal position amid rising global debt and borrowing costs.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves Rs 7,395 crore for PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana
articles.desc: Union Cabinet has allocated Rs 7,395 crore for the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana. This scheme will promote local-level capacity building and resource management for panchayats across India. Elected representatives will receive training to enhance their governance capabilities and local planning efforts. The initiative aims to financially empower panchayats through better utilization of available resources. Implementation will occur from 2026-27 to 2030-31, aligning with the Sixteenth Finance Commission period.

articles.title: Meesho loss narrows; Sanjeev Bikhchandani back as Info Edge CEO
articles.desc: Meesho cut its losses in the July-September quarter, while growth continued. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

articles.title: Chancellor begins to deliver his first Budget
articles.desc: The chancellor begins his speech by calling it a Budget for the "working people of Britain, for British businesses big and small."

articles.title: Cognite reports $1 billion in verified AI value, confirming impact of industrial AI solutions
articles.desc: Driving approximately 36% of value verified to date, customers are leveraging AI and automated workflows to prevent costly asset shutdowns across complex industrial operations, help them get back running when the unexpected happens, and lower the costs of running their operations.

articles.title: Meesho expects stronger Q3 growth due to change in festive sale timeline
articles.desc: The first day of Meesho's annual flagship sale, the Mega Blockbuster Sale, saw orders growing about 75% YoY. Its transacting customers increased by about 60% YoY.

articles.title: Sherpa and the future of AI-powered storytelling at Pocket FM
articles.desc: Pocket FM is using AI to help writers bring their stories to life and reach listeners across the world. With Sherpa, its AI-powered writing partner, the company is making it easier to manage long storylines and develop characters while keeping the creative decisions in the hands of writers.

articles.title: India, Mexico begin talks for trade pact; aim to boost commerce, investments
articles.desc: India and Mexico have initiated negotiations for a preferential trade agreement to enhance bilateral trade and investment. The agreement aims to create new economic opportunities while addressing market access, customs procedures, and trade facilitation. Discussions included organising a Mexican business mission to India in early 2027 to improve commercial ties. India had a trade surplus with Mexico, largely due to exports in autos and pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Centre open to changes in DPDP law to  protect press freedom, says Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.desc: The Centre aims to amend the Digital Personal Data Protection law to address concerns raised by news publishers. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that the law does not limit press freedom. This response follows a Supreme Court notice regarding a petition from the Digital News Publishers Association and others. Publishers argue the lack of exemption for journalism could jeopardize investigative reporting and confidential sources.

articles.title: India's industrial growth slows to 6.7% in September from 8% in August
articles.desc: India's Index of Industrial Production for September recorded a growth rate of 6.7%. This figure represents a decline from August's 8%. Key contributors to this growth include the manufacture of motor vehicles and electrical equipment, among others. The manufacture of rubber and plastics also played a significant role in September's performance. These statistics were released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

articles.desc: The BBC spoke to people in Cardiff and County Durham about their concerns ahead of the chancellor's Autumn Budget.

articles.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
articles.desc: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation.

articles.title: Former Conservative chancellor unsure Budget will 'fix big problems'
articles.desc: Sir Jeremy Hunt spoke to BBC Breakfast about his hopes and qualms ahead of John Healey's autumn Budget.

articles.title: Cabinet hikes Dearness Allowance by 3% with Rs 10,000 crore allocation; check key announcements
articles.desc: DA hike: The Union Cabinet has approved several development schemes totaling Rs 29,267 crores for various initiatives. Among these is a Rs 10,016 crore increase in Dearness Allowance for Central government employees. The DA will benefit about 48 lakh employees and 68 lakh pensioners, with hikes effective from July 1, 2026.

articles.title: Delivery Hero raises full-year forecast again on strong Q3 growth
articles.desc: The company now expects gross merchandise value (GMV), a common metric for delivery firms measuring the total value of all goods sold through the market place, to grow 10%-12% this year, up from a previous forecast of 9%-11%.

articles.title: China's new export curbs draw a line around its AI crown jewels
articles.desc: The draft rules, released on October 16, distinguish between foreign customers using Chinese AI services and foreign companies obtaining the models, data or expertise needed to operate or reproduce them independently.

articles.title: Agentic AI can cut banks' transaction monitoring workload by up to 50%: McKinsey
articles.desc: Banks could reduce the human effort required for transaction monitoring investigations by 30-50% by deploying agentic artificial intelligence (AI), while improving the quality and consistency of compliance reports, according to a report by McKinsey.

articles.title: AI chips worth $12.1 million seized at Malaysia airport, customs authority says
articles.desc: Malaysian customs said on Wednesday that it had seized about 49.5 million ringgit ($12.11 million) worth of advanced artificial intelligence chips this month, as

articles.title: India's soybean imports surge to record as domestic prices rally
articles.desc: India's soybean imports significantly increased to 1.1 million metric tons in 2025/26 compared to the previous year. Rising domestic prices prompted Indian mills to enhance their overseas purchases of soybeans. The majority of these imports originated from Niger, which became the largest exporter to India.

articles.title: China's CXMT to start advanced AI memory production despite poor yields
articles.desc: The decision highlights China's intense shortage of the AI memory chips, which are essential to a government-backed push to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's AI processors at scale amid US curbs on access to foreign-made technology.

articles.title: TPG pursues $5 billion acquisition of British data centre group Ark: FT
articles.desc: Global alternative asset manager TPG is in talks to buy British data centre group Ark from Elliott Investment Management at a valuation of about $5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: GST clarification on foreign investor brokerage offers sentiment boost, analysts say
articles.desc: The Indian government has clarified that brokerage paid by overseas clients may qualify as an export service. This could help foreign investors avoid the 18% goods and services tax on brokerage fees. Analysts suggest this clarification is sentimentally positive amid significant foreign outflows from Indian stocks. There is ongoing speculation regarding potential cuts in capital gains tax ahead of the federal budget.

articles.title: Indian IT firms poised to benefit from enterprise AI adoption as infrastructure costs rise: Report
articles.desc: Indian information technology (IT) companies are well-positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) by enterprises, as rising infrastructure investments and funding requirements increase financial risks for companies building and operating AI computing capacity, according to a research report by Anand Rathi.

articles.title: India, Mexico sign terms of reference to kickstart trade pact negotiations
articles.desc: India and Mexico have signed the Terms of Reference to initiate negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement. This agreement aims to enhance bilateral trade and investment opportunities between the two countries. Key negotiating areas include market access, customs procedures, and trade facilitation measures. Both delegations discussed organizing a Mexican business mission to India in early 2027.

articles.title: AI chip giant SK hynix says quarterly operating profit soars 630%
articles.desc: South Korean chip giant SK hynix said Wednesday its third-quarter operating profit soared 632 percent on-year, largely driven by the artificial intelligence industry's explosive demand for its advanced memory chips. The memory chip giant said it had posted record revenue and operating profit for six straight quarters since the second quarter of last year.

articles.title: Oracle's Larry Ellison dismisses 'SaaS apocalypse' fears, says AI will make software better
articles.desc: Speaking at Oracle AI World here, Ellison, the company's executive chairman and chief technology officer, rejected talk of a "SaaS apocalypse", in which businesses would use AI to build their own applications instead of buying software-as-a-service (SaaS) products.
